C: A2 [ C ] an official document that gives you permission to own, do, or use something, usually after you have paid money and/or taken a test

S or U: › [ S or U ] formal permission or freedom to do what you want
› the freedom of artists, writers, etc. to change the facts of the real world when producing art
› with special permission from the person or company who has created a product

example: a dog licence
養狗執照
a TV licence
電視（收看）許可證
As parents, they allowed their children very little licence.
作為父母，他們給孩子們的自由很少。
[ + to infinitive ] He was given licence to reform the organization.
他獲准對該組織實行改革。
It's a German product, made under licence in British factories.
這是一種經過授權在英國工廠生産的德國産品。

NONE: › a sign on a road vehicle that shows its registration number
› to give someone official permission to do or have something

example: [ + to infinitive ] Several companies have been licensed to sell these products.
一些公司獲得了這些産品的銷售許可。

NONE: › the official set of numbers and letters shown on the front and back of a road vehicle

example: You couldn't see the vehicle's license plate number.
你看不到那輛車的牌照號碼。

NONE: › a nurse in the US who has been trained to do practical nursing but who is not allowed to give medicines without permission
（美國未經許可不可接觸藥品的）執業操作護士，職業臨床護士
› a person who has official permission to do something, especially to sell alcoholic drinks
（尤指獲得酒類銷售許可的）被許可人，執照持有人
› in the UK, the laws that control when and where alcoholic drinks can be sold
› (especially of a person or their behaviour) sexual in an uncontrolled and socially unacceptable way
（尤指人或其行為）淫蕩的，放蕩的
› a grey, green, or yellow plant-like organism that grows on rocks, walls, and trees

T: B2 [ T ] to move the tongue across the surface of something

T, I + prep: › [ T,  I + prep ] If flames or waves lick something, they pass over it quickly or touch it lightly like a tongue.
（火焰）蔓延，掠過，吞捲；（波浪）拍擊，沖刷

T: › [ T ] informal to defeat easily in a competition, fight, etc.
（在競賽、爭鬥等中）輕易打敗，輕取

C: › [ C ] old-fashioned informal the act of hitting someone with something such as a whip
› [ C ] informal a small amount or thin layer
› [ C ] specialized music in jazz or rock music, a short series of notes played by one musician
（爵士樂或搖滾樂中的）小過門
› [ C ] the action of licking something

example: He licked the chocolate off his fingers.
他把手指上的巧克力舔乾淨了。
She licked the stamps and stuck them on the parcel.
她舔了一下郵票，然後貼在包裹上。
Within a few seconds flames were licking at the curtains.
幾秒鐘之內火舌就蔓延到了窗簾。
We'll lick the other teams.
我們將一舉擊敗其他球隊。
The trains go by at a hell of a lick.
火車疾馳而過。
The living room could do with a lick of paint.
客廳薄薄地刷一層油漆就行了。
Can I have a lick of your ice cream?
我可以嚐一口你的霜淇淋嗎？

NONE: › to try very hard to please someone in authority, usually in order to get an advantage
對（某人）阿諛奉承，對（某人）拍馬屁

example: He needn't expect me to go licking his boots!
他不用指望我去拍他的馬屁！

NONE: › to move your tongue along your lips
› to feel pleasure at the thought of something

example: She took a bite of doughnut and licked her lips.
她咬了一口甜甜圈，然後舔了舔嘴唇。
He licked his lips at the thought of all that money.
一想到那麽多的錢，他就有些迫不及待了。

NONE: › to spend time getting back your strength or happiness after a defeat or bad experience

S: › informal a defeat in a competition
› old-fashioned informal the punishment of being hit

example: The home team were given a good licking.
主隊輸得很慘。
